# GravHub Audit Log

Tracks holes found by `/audit` runs: incomplete features, fake/stub data presented as real,
security gaps, and silent failures. This file is meant to be edited directly — change `Status`,
add to `Notes`, or add new rows by hand at any time. Re-running `/audit` adds newly-found items
and never overwrites your edits to existing ones (matched by the finding's title).

**Status values:** `Open` · `Fixed` · `In Progress` · `Won't Fix` · `Needs Decision`

---

## Critical / High — Security & Data Integrity

| # | Finding | Location | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 82 | CRITICAL — 9 API routes had ZERO authentication and were direct paths to full account takeover: `app/api/team-members/route.ts` (GET/POST/PATCH) let anyone plant a `team_members` row with `role: 'Super Admin', isAdmin: true` for an arbitrary Gmail address, then sign in as that identity via the app's own Google Sign-In (`google-verify` finds the planted row and mints a real session — no credentials needed); `app/api/portal-clients/route.ts` (GET/POST/DELETE) leaked every client's roster and let anyone create a portal account (with `tempPassword` returned in the body) or mass-delete a company's portal users; `app/api/portal-clients/invite/route.ts` let anyone self-register a portal identity under any real client's company name and receive a working magic-link invite at an attacker email; `app/api/portal-clients/company-config/route.ts` let anyone rewrite any company's portal module visibility; `app/api/portal-clients/notifications/route.ts` had no ownership check on read/write; `app/api/portal-clients/complete-setup/route.ts` never actually validated the verification code it claimed to require, so anyone who knew/guessed a client's email could set that account's password directly; `app/api/audit-logs/route.ts` (GET/POST) exposed and let anyone forge the internal audit trail — including entries about the exploits above; `app/api/email/scheduled/route.ts` (GET/POST/DELETE) was an open phishing/spam relay through the org's verified sending domain; `app/api/portal/preview/route.ts` leaked any company's full contracts/projects/invoices/tickets to a fully unauthenticated caller | see above | Fixed | Found by an 11-agent full-app audit sweep. Added `requireAdmin`/`requireRole` to every route; `complete-setup` now requires and validates the real `verification_code` (previously collected by the UI's earlier step but never sent to or checked by this route) and clears it on use |
| 83 | HIGH — systemic pattern across the entire app: dozens of GET (read) and several POST/PATCH (write) routes had no auth check at all while their sibling routes on the same resource did, discovered independently by 8 of the 11 audit agents in modules that don't otherwise overlap. Full list by module — **CRM core**: `deals` GET/POST, `deals/[id]` PATCH, `pipelines` GET/POST (could silently rewrite the org's entire shared pipeline config), `crm/companies` POST, `crm/contacts` GET/POST, `crm/companies/[id]/files` GET/POST/DELETE (also had no file size/type validation), `crm/activities` GET, `crm/duplicates` + `/ignore`, `crm/enrich` (also a live SSRF vector — server-side fetch of a caller-supplied URL with no private-IP/localhost/cloud-metadata blocklist). **Proposals/contracts/finance**: `proposals` GET/POST, `contracts` GET/POST, `renewals` GET/POST + `[id]` PATCH, `maintenance` GET/POST + `[id]` PATCH/DELETE, `invoices` GET/POST + `[id]` PATCH, `mercury/accounts`+`/transactions` (live bank balances/transactions), `contracts/[id]/addendums` GET/POST/PATCH, `signatures` GET/POST (a real contract-forgery vector — anyone could generate a signing link for any contract to any email). **Sequences**: `sequences` GET/POST, `[id]/enroll`, `[id]/enrollments` GET/DELETE, `[id]/test-send` (real email sends), `activities`, `analytics`, `attribution`. **Social/tickets/tasks**: `social-posts` GET/POST, `[id]` GET/PATCH (no company scoping — a portal client could read or modify another company's draft posts), `[id]/publish` (no auth AND no server-side approval-status check, so a draft or rejected post could be pushed live), `tickets` GET/POST (portal-client company scoping was also entirely absent — any authenticated caller could read every company's tickets including internal-only notes), `tickets/[id]` PATCH (no ownership/field scoping), `tasks/[id]` PATCH/DELETE, `gmail/send` (any authenticated caller could send real email from any team member's connected Gmail by naming a different `userEmail` in the body — no verification the caller IS that user). **Rank tracker/monitoring**: `rank-tracker/export` (CSV of every company's keywords), `rank-tracker/keywords` GET + `[id]` GET + `[id]/history`, `rank-tracker/competitors` GET, `rank-tracker/reports` GET (leaked scheduled-report recipient emails), `tracked-keywords` GET (portal-facing — previously 401'd for every real portal-client request and was silently swallowed client-side, meaning the portal's live keyword-ranking table never showed real data at all) + `[id]` GET + `[id]/history`, `monitored-sites` GET + `[id]` GET + `[id]/check` POST + `[id]/wordpress` GET/POST (leaked WP credentials-configured status and full plugin/theme/security scan results, and let anyone trigger a live scan against any client's site) | see above | Fixed | Where a route is legitimately portal-client-facing (`proposals`, `contracts`, `invoices`, `social-posts`, `tickets`, `tracked-keywords`), added company-scoped access via `requirePortalClient` instead of a blanket staff-only gate — this also fixed the `tickets` POST/PATCH and `tracked-keywords` GET routes, which were unconditionally staff-only despite being called directly by real portal UI (ticket creation/reply, live keyword rankings), meaning those specific portal features have been silently broken (401, swallowed client-side) since they were built, independent of the security gap. `social-posts/[id]` PATCH now whitelists the exact fields the real portal approval UI sends (`approvalStatus`, `rejectionReason`), matching the pattern already established for contracts/proposals (#77). `publishSocialPost()` now refuses to publish anything with `approval_status !== 'approved'`, closing the gap where the "approval workflow" the schema comment describes was enforced only by the staff UI conditionally showing a button, not the server |
| 84 | MEDIUM — OAuth callback routes generate a CSRF `state` parameter but never validate it on return: `google-marketing/callback`, `linkedin/callback`, `meta/callback`, `drive/callback`. Since these integrations are workspace-wide singletons (one connection per product, not per-user), an attacker can complete their own OAuth consent, capture the resulting `code`/`state` redirect URL, and get a logged-in staff member to open it — silently swapping the org's Google Marketing/LinkedIn/Meta/Drive connection to the attacker's account | `app/api/integrations/google-marketing/callback/route.ts`, `app/api/integrations/linkedin/callback/route.ts`, `app/api/integrations/meta/callback/route.ts`, `app/api/drive/callback/route.ts` | Fixed | Added `lib/oauth-state.ts` — each `connect`/`auth-url` route now generates a random per-flow `state`, stamps it into a short-lived (10 min) httpOnly cookie, and passes it to the provider. Each `callback` route reads the same cookie back and rejects (redirect to an error state, cookie cleared) unless it matches the `state` query param exactly — binding the callback to the same browser that started the flow, closing the cross-account-swap path. Applied uniformly to all 4 integrations |
| 85 | LOW — `linkedin/disconnect` has no role check, unlike its siblings `google-marketing/disconnect`/`meta/disconnect` which both require `requireRole(req, 'Leadership')` — any authenticated staff member can disconnect the org's LinkedIn connection | `app/api/integrations/linkedin/disconnect/route.ts` | Fixed | Added the same `requireRole(req, 'Leadership')` gate its siblings already have |
| 86 | HIGH — the newer `/go/book/[slug]` booking system (booking types with intake questions/buffers/colors, promoted as the "Public Link" from the staff-facing Booking Types manager) was completely non-functional for real anonymous visitors — its APIs (`/api/calendar/booking-types`, `/api/calendar/bookings`) were never added to `proxy.ts`'s public-route allowlist, so every unauthenticated booking attempt 401'd. The older `/book/[slug]` flow (`calendar_settings`/`bookings` tables) was correctly public and is the one this repo's "Confirmed working" section refers to | `proxy.ts`, `app/api/calendar/booking-types/route.ts`, `app/api/calendar/bookings/route.ts` | Fixed | Added both routes to `PUBLIC_PREFIXES`. Since a prefix match can't distinguish HTTP method or query params, added route-level `requireRole` guards for the parts that must stay staff-only: `booking-types` POST (creating/editing booking types) and `bookings` GET's no-`slug`/`date` branch (the internal cross-org booking list) — the public slot-check (`slug`+`date`) and guest booking creation (POST) remain unauthenticated by design, matching the older flow |
| 87 | HIGH — `/go/review/[token]` (the public review-request page real customers get emailed) 401'd on every star-rating/feedback submission — `/api/reputation/review-request/[token]` was never added to `PUBLIC_PREFIXES`, unlike every other token-based public route (`/api/signatures/`, `/api/unsubscribe/`, `/api/proposals/view/`) | `proxy.ts` | Fixed | Added `/api/reputation/review-request/` to `PUBLIC_PREFIXES` — the route's own auth is token-only by design, matching the established pattern |

| 94 | MEDIUM — the Deal Panel's and Company Panel's "New Proposal" button opened a real, fully-functional form panel, but `onSave` discarded the collected data entirely (`onSave={(_data) => setCreatingProposal(false)}`) — clicking "Create Draft" silently closed the modal with no toast, no persistence, and no error, losing everything the user just filled in | `app/crm/pipeline/page.tsx`, `app/crm/companies/page.tsx` | Fixed | Both call sites now actually `POST /api/proposals` with the collected data (company, service type, rep, value, notes as a line item) and show a success/error toast, matching the standalone Proposals page's own create flow |
| 95 | HIGH — `app/api/crm/merge/route.ts` uses invalid PostgREST filter-path syntax (`'contact->>id'`) as if it were an update key when reassigning a merged-away contact's deals to the primary contact — the malformed call's result is never checked, so it silently fails; since `deals.contact_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, the later delete of the merged-away contact instead **nulls** the deal's contact link (rather than repointing it), and the deal card keeps showing the deleted contact's name from the stale `contact` jsonb blob. Company merge has the same root issue — `company_id` FKs on deals/contracts/invoices/projects/proposals are never repointed to the primary company, only the denormalized name string is updated, so deleting the merged-away companies nulls those FKs too | `lib/` or `app/api/crm/merge/route.ts` | Fixed | Contact merge now updates the real `deals.contact_id` FK (was targeting a nonexistent `contact->>id` column) and rewrites the `deals.contact` display blob to the primary contact's merged info. Company merge now reassigns `company_id` on deals/contracts/invoices/projects/proposals directly by id (was name-only), with a name-matched fallback restricted to rows where `company_id` is still null, so a same-named unrelated company's rows are never touched |
| 96 | MEDIUM — single-company delete (`DELETE /api/crm/companies/[id]`) only deletes the `crm_companies` row — no cascade to contacts/deals/contracts/invoices/projects/proposals/activities — directly contradicting the Companies page's own bulk-delete confirm text ("This will also remove associated contacts, deals, and contracts") and the Deal Panel's "Delete Company" button ("Remove and all its data permanently"). Only `POST /api/crm/bulk-delete`'s company path actually cascades (and only 3 of 7 related tables), and even that matches by company **name** rather than id, risking deleting an unrelated company's data if two companies share a name | `app/api/crm/companies/[id]/route.ts`, `app/api/crm/bulk-delete/route.ts` | Fixed | Explicit decision: **block, don't cascade** — irreversible data loss outweighs the inconvenience of requiring reassignment first, and this matches the codebase's one existing precedent (the pipeline stage-delete guard also blocks rather than cascades). Added `lib/crm-cascade.ts`: both delete routes now return 409 (with a message listing exactly what's still attached) if the company has any related contacts/deals/contracts/invoices/projects/proposals, matched by `company_id` FK first with a null-company_id-only name fallback (same safe pattern as the merge-route fix). The one exception is the company's own activity log — it cascades along with the company rather than blocking, since it's just interaction history with no independent value or reachable UI once the company is gone. Bulk-delete now does partial success: companies with no related records are deleted, blocked ones are skipped and reported back by name+reason, so one company with real data attached doesn't stop cleanup of the rest of the batch. Fixed a related bug found while wiring this: both the single-delete and bulk-delete frontend call sites optimistically removed companies from the UI and only caught network-level failures, never checking `res.ok` — a blocked (409) delete would have shown the company as gone in the UI while it was still fully intact server-side. Both now revert the optimistic removal and surface the real error on any non-OK response. Updated both UI surfaces' copy to describe the actual (block, not cascade) behavior |
| 97 | MEDIUM — timezone bug in the booking/calendar system: `lib/ics-generator.ts` and `lib/calendar-links.ts` (Google Calendar "Add to calendar" link) both parse a plain `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM"` string with `new Date(dateStr)`, which JS treats as the **server's local time** (UTC on Vercel) rather than the booking's configured timezone, then reformats into the target timezone — a booking intended for "2:00 PM America/Chicago" can end up on the `.ics` file/calendar link as 8:00 AM. The same root-cause bug (server-local `new Date()`/`getHours()` instead of the calendar's real timezone) also affects `lib/google-calendar.ts`'s slot-availability computation (today/lead-time cutoff, Google busy-slot day boundaries) and the calendar-sync/import routes' stored busy-time timezone stamping | `lib/ics-generator.ts`, `lib/calendar-links.ts`, `lib/google-calendar.ts`, `app/api/calendar/sync/route.ts`, `app/api/calendar/import-link/route.ts`, `app/api/calendar/subscriptions/route.ts` | Fixed | Added `lib/timezone.ts` (Intl-based, no new dependency) with `zonedWallTimeToUtc`/`dateAndTimeInZone`/`nowInZone`/`compactWallClock`, covered by new unit tests pinning known DST offsets (CDT/CST/JST) since this sandbox can't do live calendar verification. Fixed: ICS `DTSTART;TZID=` and the Google Calendar link (both already declare the zone separately, so they now just format the wall-clock digits, no conversion needed — the old round-trip through `new Date()` was the bug); the Outlook links (need a real UTC instant, now correctly converted); `computeAvailableSlots`'s today/lead-time cutoff (now reads "now" in the calendar's own configured zone, not server UTC); `getGoogleBusySlots`'s day-boundary window; and `app/api/calendar/sync/route.ts`'s Google-event-to-booking date/time extraction (feeds real availability blocking for that calendar's slug). Deliberately left `app/api/calendar/import-link/route.ts` and `app/api/calendar/subscriptions/route.ts` alone — those write to a fixed `calendar_slug: 'imported'`/subscription bucket with a self-consistent (always-UTC) timezone label that no real booking calendar's availability computation ever reads, so the inconsistency there doesn't corrupt anything customer-facing; lower priority, can revisit if that changes |

Also added the missing `requireRole('Leadership')` to `PATCH /api/broadcasts/[id]`, matching its `DELETE`/`POST /send` siblings. A/B subject testing and per-link click tracking remain unbuilt features — not touched, still need real design decisions |

| 101 | CRITICAL — `app/api/calendar/auth/route.ts` took `userEmail` directly from the request body with no check it matched the caller's own identity, then encoded it into the OAuth `state` param; `app/api/calendar/callback/route.ts` upserts `calendar_settings` keyed by that `user_email`. Any authenticated staff member could `POST` an arbitrary victim `userEmail`, complete the Google OAuth flow with their OWN Google account, and silently redirect the victim's public `/book/[slug]` link to create every future booking's Meet link/calendar event on the attacker's calendar instead — worse than the already-fixed AUDIT #84 (OAuth CSRF) since no victim interaction is required at all, the attacker drives the entire flow themselves. It rescues it at `lib/review-campaigns.ts` (selects the whole table unfiltered) and `lib/automations-engine.ts` (now `.ilike`, case-insensitive). It cannot at the three `.in('email', [...])` sites — Postgres `IN` is case-sensitive, so a mixed-case row is never returned and there is nothing to normalize. Those three are correct because the migration lowercased the table and added a CHECK constraint making such a row impossible to write; **that constraint is the guarantee, not the read-side helper**, and dropping it would silently regress all three. | 722 | MEDIUM — `lib/login-attempts.ts` (the account-lockout half of #207) held its counters in an in-process `Map`. An admin setting "Login Attempts: 3" in Security Settings therefore got materially weaker protection than the UI implies, on the three surfaces where a failure is actually observable server-side (Google Sign-In account probing, staff/portal onboarding verification codes, and the 2FA code). Table is service-role only, with deliberately no `authenticated` policy: a signed-in user has no business reading or clearing their own lockout counter. The in-process `Map` is kept as a **second** layer rather than replaced, so a database failure degrades to exactly the old behavior instead of to no protection — a caller is locked out if EITHER layer says so, and the DB read fails open (the auth lookup immediately after needs the same database anyway). All three exported functions became async; 4 call sites updated. Chose Postgres over Redis/Upstash deliberately: Supabase is already here, so no new paid dependency, and lockout only writes on FAILED attempts. **Scope note**: `proxy.ts`'s IP limiter deliberately stays in-memory — it runs in middleware on every request, so backing it with Postgres would add a DB round trip to every page load to tighten a coarse 200-req/min ceiling. 12 new tests in `tests/unit/lib/login-attempts.test.ts` pin both properties the fix exists for (lockout on a stored count with no local state; in-process enforcement preserved when the DB is unreachable). `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean, `npx eslint` clean, `npx vitest run` 558/558 passing | **Migration applied live 2026-08-05** (verified: `rate_limit_counters` table and `increment_rate_limit_counter()` both present). Drive-by fix: `inbox/unified`'s GET route had no `requireRole` call at all (relying solely on the outer proxy's authenticated-cookie-presence check, not real role verification) — added, matching every other route's convention.

Plus, fixed this pass (2026-07-16): `/reports/seo-reports`'s Recipients column had a real type/render bug — `client_integrations.seo_report_recipients` is a `text[]` column, but the frontend `Integration` interface typed it as `string | null` and rendered it directly as JSX children (`{integration.seo_report_recipients || 'Primary contact'}`). React renders array children as adjacent text nodes with no separator, so any client with 2+ recipients would have displayed as `emailoneemailtwo` with no space or comma — currently latent (nothing ever wrote to that column, since there was no edit UI), but would have surfaced silently the first time someone used the field. Fixed the type, fixed the render to join with `, `, and added an actual edit affordance (click-to-edit inline text input, comma-separated, saves via the already-existing `PATCH /api/seo-reports` `seoReportRecipients` field — the backend support existed, only the UI was missing).

An automation with no token configured can never fire regardless of what a caller sends — verified with 3 new unit tests (token matches / token mismatches / neither side has a token) alongside the existing `deal_stage_changed`/`invoice_overdue` scoping-check tests it was modeled on.

Plus, built this pass (2026-07-16, WordPress SEO plugin — user-requested feature set): the user's own punch list assumed a Schema Type selector, FAQ Q&A fields, Organization schema, a redirect manager, and a 404 monitor already existed and just needed data entered or a small enhancement added. A codebase-wide check (both the plugin and the Next.js app) found **none of these existed at all** — confirmed and surfaced to the user before building (they confirmed: build the full thing, not a stub). Built the 4 flagged-high-priority items:
- **Image sitemap**: `class-sitemap.php`'s `render_post_type_sitemap()` now declares the `xmlns:image` namespace and emits `<image:image>` entries per URL (featured image + any literal `<img>` tags in `post_content`, which covers both classic-editor HTML and Gutenberg image blocks) via a new `get_post_images()` helper, capped at 1,000 images/URL per the sitemap image-extension spec.
- **Organization + WebSite + LocalBusiness schema**: new "Organization & Local Business Schema" settings section (`class-admin-page.php`) — name/logo/sameAs for Organization+WebSite, and a checkbox-gated LocalBusiness type/address/phone. `class-meta-manager.php`'s `output_meta_tags()` was restructured so site-wide schema can print on the homepage independent of whether any page-specific meta exists (it previously bailed out entirely when there was nothing page-specific to say). Each piece is genuinely inert — prints nothing — until its own real minimum fields are filled in; nothing fabricated. LocalBusiness is opt-in (checkbox) since not every WordPress site the plugin runs on has an addressable local presence worth marking up.
- **Schema Type selector (Article/Service/FAQ) + visible FAQ accordion**: new "Schema" tab in the per-post metabox (`class-seo-metabox.php`) with a type dropdown and, for FAQ, a Q&A repeater (add/remove rows, JS-serialized to a hidden JSON field on form submit, re-validated server-side in `save_metabox()`). `class-meta-manager.php` builds real Article/Service/FAQPage JSON-LD from these fields (`build_typed_schema()`), taking priority over the older freeform API-sourced `schema_markup` when both exist. New `[gravhub_faq]` shortcode (`class-shortcodes.php`) renders the exact same `_gravhub_faq_items` post meta as a visible accordion — schema and visible content read from one field, so they can't drift out of sync the way a hand-typed schema blob with no matching UI would (the user's own stated concern, since Google increasingly wants the two to match 1:1).
- **Redirect manager + 404 monitor + fuzzy-match suggestions**: new `class-redirect-manager.php`, fully self-contained (own DB tables via `dbDelta`, own `template_redirect` hooks, own REST routes, own "Redirects" submenu page). Two new tables (`{prefix}gravhub_redirects`, `{prefix}gravhub_404_log`) created on activation and self-healed on `admin_init` the same way capabilities/cron already self-heal in this plugin (version-gated so `dbDelta` doesn't run on every request). A redirect match always wins over a 404 (checked at `template_redirect` priority 1, before WordPress's own 404 determination fully matters); an actual 404 is logged with hit-count/last-seen once the redirect check has passed. Suggestions use `similar_text()` slug-similarity against the 300 most recently modified published posts/pages — filtered in application code, not a jsonb/SQL fuzzy-match extension, kept fast enough for an on-demand click.

Verification is PHP-syntax-only (`php -l` clean on every file, both new and modified) — this environment has no live WordPress install to actually load the plugin against, so table creation, REST route behavior, and frontend rendering (accordion, redirects, sitemap image tags) are unverified beyond that. **Requires re-uploading the plugin to the client's WordPress site** to take effect (matches AUDIT #81's precedent — this repo has no build/zip step, the source PHP is the distributable) and bumps the plugin to v1.3.0. Two new Next.js endpoints follow the existing `app/api/wordpress/seo/*` pattern exactly (`requireWordPressAuth`, `?site=` → `wordpress_site_health.company_id` → `client_integrations`): `analytics/route.ts` pulls real GA4 (`getGA4Report`/`getGA4TrafficSources`/`getGA4TopPages`) and GSC (`getGSCSummary`) data, each source independently optional so a GA4-only or GSC-only client still gets an honest partial payload instead of an error; `keywords/route.ts` computes position-bucket counts (Top 3/4-10/11-20/21-50/50+) and winning/losing keyword deltas from `tracked_keywords`, ported from the same bucket logic `app/rank-tracker/page.tsx` already uses client-side. Both return `{connected: false}`/`{configured: false}` rather than zeros when a site isn't linked or isn't integrated — no fabricated numbers. **Deliberately out of scope**: Device/Age/Gender traffic breakdown (MonsterInsights-style) — confirmed via full-repo grep that zero GA4 demographic/device-dimension calls exist anywhere in this codebase; faking these would violate this project's no-fabricated-data rule, so the dashboard simply omits them rather than showing placeholder numbers. Bonus fix bundled separately: `keyword_rank_history` was missing `clicks`/`impressions` columns that `sync-gsc/route.ts` had been silently failing to write since that route was built (`add_keyword_rank_history_columns.sql`, not yet applied — sent to the user). On the plugin side: `class-api-client.php` gained `get_dashboard_analytics()`/`get_dashboard_keywords()` (15-minute transient cache, same request-boilerplate pattern as the 3 existing API methods); `class-health-reporter.php`'s `send_report()` now caches its full result to `gravhub_last_health_data` and a new `get_cheap_health_signals()` method (no live HTTP calls) exposes just the plugin/theme-update flags — both added specifically so the new dashboard's Notifications feed never has to call the 4-live-HTTP-request `collect_health_data()` synchronously on page load; `class-redirect-manager.php` gained `get_redirect_count()`/`get_404_count()` (plain `COUNT(*)`, cheap). `class-admin-page.php`'s constructor now threads `$health_reporter`/`$redirect_manager`; `render_page()` builds a `$notifications` array from real sources only (analysis issue count, cheap update signals, the last cached security-check result, live 404 count) and a shared `$modules` catalog (the original 5 toggleable modules plus 4 new purely-navigational cards — Redirections, 404 Monitor, Schema Markup, Local SEO — linking to their real pages, since none of them has a natural single on/off state). `settings-page.php` gained a Notifications feed card, the extended Modules grid, and new Site Analytics / Keywords sections that fetch `/dashboard-analytics`/`/dashboard-keywords` client-side via two new REST routes (`gravhub-seo.php`'s `rest_dashboard_analytics`/`rest_dashboard_keywords`) rather than blocking `render_page()` — those routes proxy cross-origin calls to the GravHub app that can take up to 30s on a cache miss. All rendering for the fetched sections builds DOM nodes via `textContent` (not `innerHTML` string interpolation) to avoid any XSS surface from keyword/page-title text. **Verification**: `php -l` clean on all 6 touched/new PHP files; `tsc --noEmit`, `next build`, and the full `vitest` suite (156 tests) all pass. Plus, verified during the 2026-08-07 optimistic-delete sweep (the #294 / #106 class — a row dropped from local state on DELETE, with no restore when the request fails). This class regressed twice, so it earned a re-check rather than being trusted: all **37** call sites across `app/` and `components/` were enumerated and each one's failure path read. Every one reverts correctly. Worth recording two things so the next sweep doesn't redo it. First, the naive detector flags `app/crm/delivery-dashboard/page.tsx` as missing a revert, and that is a false positive on the *best-written* site of the 37 — it deliberately avoids restoring a `prev` snapshot (which would discard a concurrent success that landed mid-flight) and instead reinserts the removed row at its original index via a functional update, guarded against double-insert. Restoring a snapshot is the obvious-looking pattern and the subtly wrong one. Second, the sites split into two correct idioms — snapshot-restore where nothing else mutates the list, and index-reinsert where something might — so a future guard for this class cannot simply require one shape.

Plus, verified during the 2026-08-07 API-response-shape sweep (the #567 / #600 class — an API response consumed as an array without checking it is one, so an error body reaches `.map()` and white-screens the page). **Clean, and the reasons are two deliberate design decisions worth knowing before anyone re-runs this.** First, `paginatedJson` returns the **bare array** and puts the cursor in an `X-Next-Cursor` *header* rather than wrapping the body in `{data, nextCursor}`. That single choice is why all 51 raw `fetch()` calls against the 31 paginated routes are safe — there is no `{data}` envelope to forget to unwrap, which is the usual form of this bug. Second, `apiFetch`/`apiFetchPage` in `lib/supabase.ts` already does `Array.isArray(data) ? data : []`, plus retry-with-backoff on retryable statuses and an empty-array fallback on a non-ok response, so every `fetchCrmContacts`-style helper is guarded at the source. A scan for unguarded array state produces three apparent hits (`crm/companies`, `crm/contacts`, `finance`) and **all three are false positives**: the first two call those guarded helpers, and the third has a full `r.ok` check that throws, sitting further back than a naive look-behind window reaches. Also swept in the same pass and clean: `app/api/**` routes with no authentication reference (36 candidates, every one either deliberately public — webhooks, share tokens, public forms, tracking pixels — or authenticated via a helper the regex missed, such as `requireExtensionToken`).

Plus, verified during the 2026-08-07 **runtime** pass — the first time this app has been started and crawled rather than only read. Method, recorded because it needs no credentials and is repeatable: write a `.env.local` whose `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` points at an unreachable address, start the server, and crawl. Every database call then fails, so the crawl exercises each page's *failure* path rather than its happy path. Results: **all 83 static page routes returned 200** — no server-side crash anywhere — and the dev log contained no React render error across the whole crawl, only a Sentry deprecation warning. Of 45 API routes probed, 32 correctly 401'd, 9 405'd, and the single 500 was `calendar/booking-types`, which is intentionally public (#253) and whose error body is sanitised in production (confirmed live against a real production build: `{"error":"Internal server error"}`). Two apparent findings were run down and both are already-adjudicated deliberate decisions, not defects: `/api/auth/health` is unauthenticated **on purpose** (#242 removed the real secret-fragment disclosure and kept the presence check public so a broken auth system can still be diagnosed), and the raw `TypeError` visible in dev is exactly what `withErrorHandler` is designed to show outside production. The one genuine gap this surfaced was in the tests rather than the app — see #771.
